content.comment_body: Hello, I have connected my system to the SolarEdge device using the correct port and Modbus ID, and I am using the same VM settings as you. Could you share a sample program block? I am unsure how to create code for displaying these values on the LCD screen. When I tried to use a floating point converter block, the result shows 0.00. Which block is appropriate for accessing VM 30 and other values? I found all addresses listed on page 17 of this document, and once I get the first value working, I plan to try others. [url]

Just as a note, you posted in the German section of the forum. A moderator will likely move your topic to the English section on Monday. Regarding your question: The referenced registers in SolarEdge use the Int16 format. These values can be read using a simple network analog input block.

Apologies for posting in the wrong forum section, I found the discussion via Google. Thanks for the example; indeed, I used the incorrect block previously. I tested your program, entering my IP and ID, but still no data appears on my system, so there may be an issue with the Modbus setup. I have three batteries at home connected via RS485 Modbus to the inverter. Could this setup cause problems? I heard that Modbus typically supports only one active connection at a time. I realize this isn’t a system-specific issue.
I am unable to provide advice on this matter since I am not familiar with the SolarEdge hardware.

Hi, after several attempts I discovered that Modbus was not enabled on the inverter. Here are steps to activate Modbus TCP on a SolarEdge inverter: 1. Enable WiFi direct by switching the red toggle on the inverter to 'P' for less than 5 seconds. 2. Connect to the inverter’s access point like a normal WiFi network; the password is posted on the right side of the inverter. 3. Open a browser and visit http://172.16.0.1 then select 'Site Communication'. From this page, Modbus TCP can be enabled without requiring the installer account or dedicated app. Ensure the port is set (default is 1502—this is adjustable). Now it works! Source: [url]

For reading Modbus values from SolarEdge: the Modbus address is '40084' (which I forgot to mention earlier). Make sure your SolarEdge device is configured to a fixed IP address. For older inverters, you must open the front panel and access the settings menu to activate Modbus functionality.
